blocks.text: 1 Introduction

Retrieval quality bounds the quality of retrieval-augmented answers: if the relevant passage is not retrieved, the generator cannot cite it. This section motivates the comparison and states the research questions.

blocks.text: 2 Related work
Prior work compares sparse and dense retrievers on open-domain question answering, but few studies hold the reader model fixed while varying only the retriever.

chunks.text: Prior work compares sparse and dense retrievers on open-domain question answering, but few studies hold the reader model fixed while varying only the retriever.

blocks.text: 3 Method
We describe the retrievers, the indexing settings, and how passages are scored and merged before they are passed to the reader.

chunks.text: We describe the retrievers, the indexing settings, and how passages are scored and merged before they are passed to the reader.

blocks.text: 4 Experiments
All experiments use the same reader model and the same passage budget so that differences can be attributed to retrieval.

blocks.text: 5 Results
We report top-20 accuracy and nDCG@10 for every configuration; confidence intervals come from 1,000 bootstrap samples.

blocks.text: 6 Discussion
The results suggest that lexical and semantic signals are complementary, but the size of the gain depends on the question type.
